name: Anime painterly background
name_th: ฉากหลังอนิเมะแบบวาดสี
historical_background: Hand-painted backgrounds for Japanese TV and film animation were traditionally made in opaque poster colour on paper and photographed under cels; since the 2000s most are painted digitally while keeping the brushy, opaque look. (Artistic overview; no history page opened.)
visual_characteristics: Detailed, lush environments behind simpler cel characters: towering cumulus skies, sunlit streets, overgrown greenery, glowing windows.
line_characteristics: Almost no outlines in the background; edges are painted, crisp on architecture and soft on foliage and clouds.
shape_language: Big readable masses (sky, hill, building) broken into many small leaf and cloud clusters; perspective-correct man-made forms.
color_characteristics: Saturated but natural: deep cerulean skies, warm cream highlights, cool blue-violet shadows; strong warm/cool temperature shifts.
lighting_characteristics: Clear sun direction, bright rim on clouds, soft bounce, light shafts and lens bloom; time of day drives the whole palette.
texture_characteristics: Gouache-like opaque strokes, soft gradients in sky, small dry-brush flecks on foliage; no grain or photo texture.
composition_characteristics: Wide establishing shots, low horizon to show sky, strong leading lines of streets or rails, room left for a character.
emotional_characteristics: Nostalgic, hopeful, summery, quietly lonely or wonder-filled.
time_optic_fit: Good for story-clip backdrops (e.g. the shop street at dusk) and calm carousel backgrounds; never for the product itself. A real frame cutout can sit on such a background only if lighting direction is matched.
common_mistakes: characters rendered in the same painterly detail so they sink into the background
over-saturated sky that kills the subject
prompt_template: Hand-painted animation background of {subject} in {setting}, opaque gouache-like brushwork, crisp painted architecture, soft clustered foliage, towering clouds, {palette}, {lighting}, {composition}, no characters unless stated, no text.
prompt_example: Hand-painted animation background of a small corner eyewear shop with a glowing window in a narrow Bangkok soi, opaque gouache-like brushwork, crisp painted shutters, soft clustered potted plants, towering pink clouds, warm cream and cerulean with Phthalo green shop sign shape (no letters), golden hour light from the left, low horizon with leading lines of the street, no characters, no text.
avoid_phrases: titles of copyrighted films, games or series
flux_notes: FLUX schnell produces convincing painterly skies and streets; it tends to add stray signage text (say 'no text, blank signs') and sometimes adds characters.

name: Chibi / kawaii
name_th: ชิบิ / คาวาอี้
historical_background: Kawaii ('cute') aesthetics became a mainstream Japanese visual culture from the 1970s onward, and 'chibi' super-deformed proportions (very large head, tiny body) became a standard comic and merchandise convention. (Artistic overview; no history page opened.)
visual_characteristics: Characters 2–3 heads tall, oversized heads and eyes, tiny hands and feet, rosy cheeks, simple expressions; props shrunk to toy-like scale.
line_characteristics: Clean rounded outlines of even or gently tapered weight, often slightly thicker outer contour.
shape_language: Circles and soft rounded rectangles; no sharp angles; bean-shaped bodies.
color_characteristics: Pastels and candy colours with a few saturated accents; white highlights in eyes; pink blush.
lighting_characteristics: Flat or one-step cel shading, soft glow, sparkle effects.
texture_characteristics: Smooth flat fills, sometimes subtle paper or soft airbrush gradient.
composition_characteristics: Centered single character or a tight cluster, generous negative space, stickers and icons around.
time_optic_fit: Fits kids' frames and playful tips (e.g. 'clean your lenses'); a chibi character can wear a simplified frame icon, but real product shots must stay the real photo next to it.
common_mistakes: adult proportions with just big eyes
hands with five detailed fingers drawn badly
drawing a real frame model in chibi form and implying it is the product
prompt_template: Cute chibi character of {subject}, 2.5 heads tall, oversized head and eyes, tiny hands, rounded clean outlines, flat cel colour with soft blush, {setting}, {palette}, {lighting}, {composition}, plain background, no text.
prompt_example: Cute chibi optometrist girl holding a giant pair of round glasses, 2.5 heads tall, oversized head and sparkly eyes, tiny hands, rounded clean outlines, flat cel colour with soft blush, standing in a tiny toy-like shop, pastel peach and snow with Phthalo green accent, soft even light, centered with negative space, plain background, no text.
avoid_phrases: titles of copyrighted films, games or series

name: Rubber-hose cartoon (1920s–30s)
name_th: การ์ตูนแขนสายยาง ยุค 1920–30
historical_background: Rubber-hose animation was the dominant style of American cartoons of the 1920s and early 1930s: bendy, boneless limbs, pie-cut eyes, white gloves; it is credited to animator Bill Nolan in silent-era shorts and faded by the mid-1930s as studios moved to more realistic movement (Cartoon Brew).
visual_characteristics: Bouncy black-and-white (or limited colour) characters with noodle arms, round bodies, pie-cut eyes, white gloves and big shoes; everything squashes and stretches.
line_characteristics: Bold, smooth ink lines of fairly even weight; limbs drawn as single flowing curves with no elbows or knees.
shape_language: Circles and tubes; bodies like balls or pears; props alive with faces.
color_characteristics: Black, white and greys, or faded early two-strip-like colour (muted red, teal, cream); aged-film feel.
lighting_characteristics: Flat lighting, small drop shadows under feet, no modelled shading.
texture_characteristics: Film grain, gate weave, slight vignette, paper-cel flatness.
composition_characteristics: Stage-like side view, characters centred, simple repeating backgrounds, iris-in/out framing.
time_optic_fit: Good for a retro mascot or gag about lost glasses; keep product out of the cartoon or place the real cutout beside it. Strongly vintage, so use sparingly.
common_mistakes: too-clean digital lines with no film texture
prompt_template: 1920s–30s rubber-hose cartoon of {subject}, boneless noodle limbs, pie-cut eyes, white gloves, bold even ink lines, {setting}, {palette}, {lighting}, {composition}, film grain and slight vignette, no text.
prompt_example: 1920s–30s rubber-hose cartoon of a cheerful pair of glasses with tiny noodle legs dancing on a shop counter, boneless limbs, pie-cut eyes, white gloves, bold even ink lines, simple shop backdrop, black white and warm cream, flat light with drop shadow, centered stage view with iris vignette, film grain, no text.
avoid_phrases: titles of copyrighted films, games or series
flux_notes: FLUX gets the look roughly but often adds modern shading or invents known mascots; name traits (pie-cut eyes, noodle limbs) rather than eras alone.

visual_characteristics: High-contrast ink drawings dominated by solid blacks, rain, cigarette smoke, slatted shadows, hard faces.
line_characteristics: Heavy brush inks, bold silhouettes, little hatching; shapes defined by black masses rather than lines.
shape_language: Angular, sharp shapes; tall verticals of buildings; harsh triangles of light.
color_characteristics: Black and white, sometimes one spot colour (red, yellow, or brand green).
lighting_characteristics: Hard single sources, venetian-blind shadows, streetlights, underlight; deep cast shadows.

composition_characteristics: Dramatic angles, tilted frames, tight close-ups, silhouettes in doorways.

line_characteristics: Clean or slightly textured lines; often no lines, just shapes.

color_characteristics: Limited palette of 3–5 colours, bold contrast between metaphor and ground.
lighting_characteristics: Flat or soft graphic shading; light used symbolically.
